post_text:
Mandarin Oriental no longer has a Food & Beverage department.

On 3 November, @Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group turned F&B into Restaurants, Bars & Experiences, or RB&E. Restaurants and bars stop being hotel "outlets". They are run as destinations in their own right.

The new division is led by @Christian Gradnitzer, Group Director RB&E. Trained in Austria, then at The Dorchester and Burj Al Arab, he helped build Jumeirah's restaurants and bars division in 2014. He joined Group CEO @Laurent Kleitman's team in 2025. @James Norman now runs RB&E operations for Europe and the Americas.

The starting point is strong: 33 Michelin stars, from @Chef Fei's two-star The Bay in Shenzhen to OPUS by @Alessio Durante. Hong Kong leads the change, with 14 venues reworked in phases, starting with The Pizza Bar by @Daniele Cason and the whisky salon Thistle & Jade.

The signal: a hotel restaurant is now judged like any stand-alone address in town. Gradnitzer's line: "Craft differentiates us, but execution earns trust."

Should hotel restaurants still be run as a hotel department, or as stand-alone businesses?

Read the full article: https://hospitality-signals.com/signal-of-the-week/2026-11-06-mandarin-oriental-restaurants-bars-experiences/
